ai.title: Document .codebuffignore negation rules in FAQ
ai.summary: Added section to web/src/content/help/faq.mdx detailing .codebuffignore negation syntax. Explains standard .gitignore negation rules for un-ignoring files. Includes examples for nested directory negation constraints. Clarifies precedence: .gitignore content processed first, then .codebuffignore.

eli5.text: The help documentation now explains how to tell Codebuff to pay attention to specific files even if your project is set to ignore them by default. This affects anyone writing or reading the help guide, who previously couldn't find guidance on selectively un-ignoring files. You'd notice by seeing new step-by-step examples showing how to use a special rule to override ignored-file settings, including a note that parent folders must be un-ignored before files inside them can be re-included.

ai.title: Fix terminal command output parsing
ai.summary: The `runCommandPty` function in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` was updated to correctly parse command output by buffering data and identifying the prompt identifier (`PS1`/`PS2`) more robustly. The previous logic for stripping the initial command echo and detecting the end of output was replaced with a stateful buffer that tracks the prompt suffix and remaining echo lines, preventing premature termination or output corruption. This change ensures accurate stdout capture and proper command completion detection in persistent PTY sessions.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a command in your terminal, the tool now captures what the command prints more reliably, so multi-step results and long outputs appear complete instead of getting cut off or jumbled. You will see fewer cases where a command's output disappears or stops early, which means you get the full answer from whatever you ask the assistant to run.

ai.title: Add analytics for checkpoints, modes, models, platform
ai.summary: New analytics events track checkpoint commands (`cli.checkpoint_command_used`) and enrich app launch/login events with `platform`, `costMode`, `model`, and `version`. `npm-app/src/client.ts` imports `os` and `package.json` to attach these properties to `APP_LAUNCHED` and user identification logs. `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts` adds a `DEBUG_DEV_EVENTS` flag to console-log events in non-production. Scope: `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`, `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, `npm-app/src/client.ts`, `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts`.

eli5.text: When you open the app, the service now records which operating system you're on, what pricing plan and AI model you've selected, and which version of the app you're running. When you use the undo or redo checkpoint commands, that action is also logged with the exact command you typed. These new tracking events and extra details are already active today in the live app; the only addition not yet triggered is a developer console-logging flag that is turned off by default.

ai.title: Add WINDOWS.md for Windows dev setup
ai.summary: Added WINDOWS.md documenting Windows development environment setup. File contains shared machine access instructions via Shadow.tech, credentials, and installation steps using Chocolatey and NVM. Internal documentation only, no code changes.

eli5.text: If you need to work on projects for this company from a Windows computer, there's now a step-by-step guide explaining how to set up your environment. The guide includes login details and access information for a shared Windows machine, as well as instructions for installing necessary tools using an automated package manager. This document is only for internal team members and doesn't change anything in the main software, it's just a new reference file to help developers get started more easily.

ai.title: Windows dev doc list format
ai.summary: Windows dev setup guide credentials section converted to bullet list. No functional change. Affects WINDOWS.md.

eli5.text: The list of login details in the Windows setup guide was reformatted from plain lines into bullet points, so the shared Windows machine credentials section now reads as a tidy list instead of a block of text. This only changes how the information looks; nothing you type or click works differently because of it. If you open the Windows setup guide and look at the credentials section, you'll see the same email and passwords arranged with small bullets in front of each line. The change is live now in the guide.
